i0: In a **passive** sentence, the person or thing that the action happens **to** becomes the subject: *The bridge **was built** in 1932.* We don't need to say who built it.
i1: The passive is made with **be** + **past participle**, in any tense: *is made, was made, has been made, will be made*. Compare the active: *Engineers **built** the bridge in 1932.*
pv-present.t: Present simple passive: is made, are sold
pv-present.s: **am / is / are + past participle**: *Cheese **is made** from milk. These phones **are made** in Korea.*
pv-present.b1: Use *is* with a singular subject and *are* with a plural subject. Then add the **past participle** (*made, spoken, cleaned*).
pv-present.b2: Negative and questions work like *be*: *Breakfast **isn't included**. **Is** breakfast **included**?*
pv-past.t: Past simple passive: was built, were invited
pv-past.s: **was / were + past participle**: *The castle **was built** in 1450. We **were invited** to the wedding.* Add **by** to say who did it.
pv-past.b1: Use ***was*** with *I / he / she / it* and ***were*** with *you / we / they*: *The car **was repaired**. The cars **were repaired**.*
pv-past.b2: Add ***by*** + the person or thing only when it's important to say who did it: *The telephone **was invented by** Bell.*
pv-use-by.t: When do we use the passive? And when do we need by?
pv-use-by.s: Use the passive when **who does it** is unknown, obvious or unimportant, or when we want to focus on the **action or result**. Use **by** only when the agent adds useful information.
pv-use-by.b1.0: we **don't know** who did it: *My wallet **has been stolen**.*
pv-use-by.b1.1: it's **obvious** or **unimportant**: *The rubbish **is collected** on Mondays.* (by the council, obviously)
pv-use-by.b1.2: we want to **focus** on the thing, not the person: *This song **was written** in 1965.*
pv-use-by.b1.3: in **formal, scientific or news** writing: *The samples **were heated** to 100°C.*
pv-use-by.b2: Leave out *by* + agent when it says nothing new: *The thief **was arrested*** (not *by the police*, which is obvious). Keep it when it's important: *The film **was directed by** a 19-year-old.*
pv-use-by.b3: Don't overuse the passive. In everyday speech, the active is usually more natural: *Someone stole my bike* or *My bike was stolen* are both fine; *My bike was stolen by someone* is not natural.
pv-use-by.n2: focus on the action, not the person
pv-continuous-perfect.t: Continuous and perfect passives: is being done, has been done
pv-continuous-perfect.s: Continuous: **is / was being + past participle**. Perfect: **has / had been + past participle**: *The road is being repaired. My bike has been stolen.*
pv-continuous-perfect.b0.3.2: *The house **had been sold** before we saw it.*
pv-continuous-perfect.b1: Choose the tense as you would for an active sentence, then make it passive with a form of ***be*** + past participle.
pv-modals.t: Future and modal passives: will be done, can be done, must be done
pv-modals.s: After **will, can, must, should, might**, use **be + past participle**: *The results will be announced tomorrow. This can't be done.*
pv-modals.b1: The pattern is always ***modal + be + past participle***: *will be built, can be seen, must be paid, might be cancelled*.
pv-modals.b2: *Be going to* works the same way: *The match **is going to be shown** on TV.*
pv-modals.b3: For the past, use ***modal + have been + past participle***: *It **should have been fixed** last week.* *The letter **might have been lost**.*
q.pv-use-by-s01: Which sentence uses the passive most naturally?
x.pv-use-by-s01: The agent is unknown or obvious: no *by*.
q.pv-use-by-s02: In which sentence is the *by* phrase useful?
x.pv-use-by-s02: *By a famous architect* adds new, useful information.
